observed_evidence: Reuters reported on September 15 that Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis launched a new wave of attacks on Saudi Arabia, saying they fired dozens of missiles and drones at the Khamis Mushait military airbase; the Saudi-led coalition said 13 civilians were wounded.

Reuters reported Houthi forces had taken Perim Island at the mouth of the Red Sea and maintained effective control over almost the entire western coast of Yemen, while Saudi and Yemeni air forces increased strikes on Houthi positions.

The Saudi East-West oil pipeline remained offline with no announced restart date. Reuters cited traders saying a prolonged shutdown could cut off as much as 4% of global oil supply while Hormuz remains largely blockaded; this 4% figure is an industry estimate, not an official production series.
Planned Gulf Arab-Iran talks on reopening Hormuz remained postponed. Reuters reported the IRGC continued to state that the strait was closed and under its control.
September 14 crude settlements were Brent $105.68/bbl and WTI $101.39/bbl after intraday gains of nearly 5%.
semantic_interpretation: The conflict has broadened from Hormuz and the Saudi bypass pipeline into a simultaneous Red Sea/Bab el-Mandeb security problem. Control of Perim Island and renewed Saudi-Houthi strikes increase the persistence of shipping, insurance, freight and delivered-energy risk even if individual oil-price spikes partially reverse. This is semantic interpretation only.
